trickyParts: Item 8's take-over wait retries 'no live session' too, so a send to a session that is really gone reads failed about 12 s after its first try, and a request that sends during a take-over answers up to ~12 s later (up to ~22 s against a listener that hangs every read). Browser specs that assert a failed send were given their own timeouts naming listenerTakeoverWindow; 7 affected specs pass on chromium in the pod.

Item 7 departs from the plan's 400 above 8000 bytes for a published frame: the browser suite's agent-view specs publish ~12.4 KB replays, so a call is split into parts under 7900 bytes sent in one transaction and reassembled on every process; a frame that is not valid UTF-8 is refused 400 FRAME_INPUT.
A person's Retry beside a live claim still opens its own attempt (existing rule); claim renewal during the take-over wait keeps the resume loop off the attempt, not a Retry.
A GitHub installation token keeps its rate-limit scope until it expires, so a caller holding a token minted before a refresh is still gated.

A listener failure is retried only when the client marks it ErrUnreachable (transport failure, 502/503/504); every other non-200 stays ErrUnavailable for the callers that read only that, and is recorded as 'envoy listener answered: …', which is not retried.
Importer compare-and-set uses the row's xmin (every write by any build changes it); resolve()'s own installation-id write carries the new xmin so it does not supersede its own sync.
A comment's concurrent mention senders each take their own transaction-tracking mark (store.ForConcurrentRead); sharing the request's mark made the pool refuse a second connection under load.
deviations: Item 7 frame limit: chunked notifications instead of a 400 above 8000 bytes (the agent-view browser specs publish ~12 KB replays).
Held rate-limit error text names when the limit was recorded (updated_at), not its end time: the tester's test moves `until` between syncs, and a new or extended limit still changes the text.

A comment whose issue has a route, which replies to a thread, or which is on a document waits out a take-over before it commits (up to the 12 s window), so the route fan-out decision is made on a real listener answer; a comment with none of those commits at once and its senders wait under their claims.

A comment.created payload gains `mentions_decide_routes` (omitempty): whether the comment fans out beyond its mentions (route, thread reply, document), recorded at commit so a resumed or retried mention knows its pre-commit resolution was final.

Replacing commentClaimMode with one bound-attempt int changes one rare state: if a Retry settled attempt 1 before the creating claim while a later attempt k is pending, the creating send now reports attempt 1 and leaves k to the resume loop instead of sending k itself.

The tester's comment_mention_takeover_test.go changes in one line only, its server construction, so TestACommentMentioningSeveralEndedSessionsAnswersWithinOneTakeOverWindow keeps the real 12 s window now that the rig defaults to 750 ms; no assertion changed.
